汉字 Hanzi Atlas frequency flashcards

1,500 hanzi · 3,000 words · 100 radicals · 86 components

Ranked by real corpus frequency. Hanzi 1–1500 use Jun Da's Modern Chinese Character Frequency List, with stroke counts, radicals, and component decomposition cross-checked against a stroke-sum consistency test (each component set is only shown if its strokes actually add up to the character's real stroke count). Words 1–1000 come from the original curated list; words 1001–3000 are ranked by frequency in a large news corpus (via the jieba segmentation dictionary) and defined via CC-CEDICT. Every hanzi card shows its component breakdown right on the front — the building blocks you'd use for a Heisig-style mnemonic story — before you ever flip to see pinyin and meaning. Word cards break down the same way: each word shows the hanzi it's built from, and each of those hanzi still shows its own sub-components. Flashcards shuffle from a weighted frequency pool — the top 20 hanzi surface far more often than characters ranked 1481–1500.

Frequency pool weighting

rank 1rank 1500

How the weighting works: the 1,500 hanzi are split into 75 pools of 20 (ranks 1–20, 21–40, …, 1481–1500). For each pool, we take the median of the raw corpus frequency counts of its 20 characters, then convert that into a relative sampling weight against the least-frequent pool. Pool 1 ends up roughly –× more likely to appear when you shuffle in Weighted mode than pool 75. The 3,000 words are weighted with a modeled Zipf curve (no raw corpus counts exist for them). Switch to True random mode in Flashcards for a flat, unweighted shuffle instead.
